meta.title: Trade Small Tasks for Free - A Plain-English Directory
meta.disclaimer: Every listing below aims to be free to join and free to use. Owners change their rules without warning; always confirm on the site itself. Nothing here is a paid listing and no personal data is collected by this page.

cards.title: Front Porch Forum
cards.blurb: A free neighborhood email digest. You post one short note ("I'll trade guitar help for weeding") and it goes to nearby subscribers. Popular in Vermont and beyond.
cards.who_for: Neighbors who want a gentle, moderated way to ask for and offer help.
cards.how_to_join: Sign up with your street address on the site to get your local digest. Posting is done via email or web form.
cards.notes: Free for residents; some areas may have limited coverage.

cards.title: Nextdoor (free tier)
cards.blurb: A neighborhood social network with a free "Recommendations" and "For Sale & Free" section where task swaps happen all day long.
cards.who_for: People who already have (or can verify) an address in a covered neighborhood.
cards.how_to_join: Download the app or use the website, verify your address, join your neighborhood feed, then post in the free tier sections.
cards.notes: Core posting is free. Ads and optional paid upgrades exist; you can ignore all of them.

cards.title: Craigslist "community" and "free" sections
cards.blurb: The old classic still works: a local "community" board where folks post "free labor for help moving books" style offers.
cards.who_for: People comfortable with a bare-bones, unmoderated classifieds vibe.
cards.how_to_join: Pick your city, browse "community" or "free", post with a reply-to email alias.
cards.notes: Posting in community sections is free; some job categories charge. Stay in the free ones.

cards.title: Your town library's community board
cards.blurb: Public libraries nearly always have a corkboard or glass case by the entrance for local events, skill offers, and help-wanted (unpaid) notes.
cards.who_for: Anyone who prefers paper, pushpins, and being surprised.
cards.how_to_join: Walk in, ask at the front desk about posting rules, pin a card with your offer or ask.
cards.notes: Rules vary: some want a phone number, some just want an email. Use contact details you are okay making public.

cards.title: Coffee shop, co-op, and community-center boards
cards.blurb: Independent cafes, food co-ops, gyms, and rec centers usually keep a bulletin board near the counter or restrooms.
cards.who_for: People who want hyper-local reach without going online at all.
cards.how_to_join: Ask the staff or manager for permission, follow their posting rules (often a business card + tear-off tabs).
cards.notes: This link is a search shortcut, not a specific venue. Pick your own local spots.

cards.title: Buy Nothing Project groups
cards.blurb: Hyper-local gift-economy groups (on Facebook and via the official app) where everything, including help, is given freely. No selling, no trading required.
cards.who_for: Anyone who wants to give or receive without money ever entering the picture.
cards.how_to_join: Search for your local Buy Nothing group on the platform you already use, or use their official app lookup.
cards.notes: Free by design. Members often post "can anyone help me..." requests.

cards.title: Facebook local groups (search "[Your Town] community")
cards.blurb: Almost every town has a free community group where neighbors trade favors, ride-shares, and tutoring sessions.
cards.who_for: People already on Facebook who want the biggest local pool.
cards.how_to_join: Search Facebook for your town name + "community" or "neighbors", request to join, read pinned rules, post your ask.
cards.notes: Groups are free to join and keep your personal profile private to friends if you set that up.

cards.title: Library skill-swap / skill-share nights
cards.blurb: Many public libraries run a free evening where residents teach each other short sessions: a guitar chord, a spreadsheet trick, a sewing stitch.
cards.who_for: Anyone who learns better in person and wants to teach something small.
cards.how_to_join: Call or check your library's events calendar. If there is no swap night, ask a librarian if one can start; librarians love this idea.
cards.notes: Free; some branches ask you to register online so they can count attendance.

cards.title: Local university / community-college message boards
cards.blurb: Community colleges often have a public-facing events board or community education office; students also tutor neighbors for free through volunteer clubs.
cards.who_for: People near a campus who want study buddies or beginner tutoring.
cards.how_to_join: Visit the college's community programs or student-life page; email the volunteer center and ask what's open to the public.
cards.notes: This links to one example college; search for the community college nearest you instead.

cards.title: Senior centers and YMCA community classes
cards.blurb: Many senior centers and Y locations host free community classes and often welcome volunteer helpers teachers.
cards.who_for: People of any age; great for retirees who want to keep teaching.
cards.how_to_join: Check the center's newsletter or front desk for a volunteer-teacher sign-up.
cards.notes: Classes for participants are usually free or low-cost; volunteering to teach or help is always free.

cards.title: Local tool library or lending library of things
cards.blurb: Community tool libraries lend drills, sewing machines, ladders, and lawn gear for free; most also list members who are happy to show you how to use something.
cards.who_for: Renters, beginners, and anyone who does not want to own a sander.
cards.how_to_join: Search the Local Tools map for one near you, bring a photo ID and proof of local address, sign up as a member.
cards.notes: Most are free; a few charge a tiny annual fee, which they post on their site - check before you go.

cards.title: Repair Cafes
cards.blurb: Volunteer-run events where fixers meet broken things. Free repairs, free tea, and free lessons in how things work.
cards.who_for: Anyone with a wobbly lamp and two free hours; and the fixers who'd love to teach you.
cards.how_to_join: Use the global repair cafe map to find one near you. To help instead of bring, email the local organizer from the listing.
cards.notes: Free; donations to cover materials are welcome but optional.

cards.title: Little Free Library and Little Free Pantry boxes
cards.blurb: Free standing book boxes and pantry boxes on street corners run by neighbors. The book kind doubles as a place to leave a note offering a skill.
cards.who_for: Neighbors walking past; backpackers; book hoarders.
cards.how_to_join: None needed - just walk by, take a book, leave a book, attach a laminated note if the steward allows it.
cards.notes: Free forever by design.

cards.title: Mutual Aid Hub directory
cards.blurb: A volunteer-maintained national map of local mutual-aid groups that match requests for small tasks (rides, groceries, tech help) with volunteers.
cards.who_for: People who want organized, no-strings-asked help with real-life logistics.
cards.how_to_join: Click your state or city on the map, use the "join" or "request" link on the local group's own page.
cards.notes: Volunteer-run; response times vary by area.

cards.title: Community fridge / pantry networks
cards.blurb: Neighborhood fridges and pantries are staffed by volunteer networks who often need help with pickups, restocking, and rides.
cards.who_for: Both people who need a hand and people who want to give one.
cards.how_to_join: Search a community fridge map or a local Facebook group; message the stewards about helping.
cards.notes: Free. Food safety rules vary by city - read the network's guidelines first.

cards.title: Time banks (hOurworld / local chapters)
cards.blurb: Trade hours, not dollars: one hour of dog-walking earns one hour of guitar lessons. Time banks track it all for you.
cards.who_for: Anyone who wants the tidy fairness of hour-for-hour exchange.
cards.how_to_join: Search for a local time bank (hOurworld hosts many), request an account, meet the orientation buddy.
cards.notes: Membership is usually free; a few chapters collect small dues, which they list plainly.

cards.title: VolunteerMatch
cards.blurb: The giant searchable database of nonprofit volunteer needs - technical help, translation, tutoring, event setups.
cards.who_for: People who want a concrete, single-commit volunteer task and match it to a real organization.
cards.how_to_join: Create a free account (name + email), set your city, filter by cause and time commitment, apply to one listing.
cards.notes: Free for volunteers. Nonprofits pay for extra features; you will never see that side.

cards.title: Points of Light / HandsOn network affiliates
cards.blurb: Local HandsOn centers run scheduled volunteer projects, often one-day task events like park cleanups or school supply packing.
cards.who_for: People who like showing up to a pre-organized event, not managing their own project.
cards.how_to_join: Find your local affiliate through the network's locator and sign up for an upcoming project.
cards.notes: Free. Some one-off events ask you to pay nothing more than your attendance.

cards.title: Reddit local subreddits (r/[YourCity], r/[YourState])
cards.blurb: Every decent-sized city has a subreddit where people swap task help, moving crews, and tutoring leads in the free-tier comments.
cards.who_for: Lurkers ready to finally post something nice.
cards.how_to_join: Create a free throwaway-ish account, find your city's subreddit by searching "reddit + your city", read the rules, post.
cards.notes: Free. Some subreddits restrict new accounts; build a bit of comment history first.

cards.title: Meetup "skill exchange" and "barter" groups
cards.blurb: Search Meetup for "skill exchange", "barter", or "trading post" - several cities have groups that meet monthly just to swap knowledge.
cards.who_for: People who want a standing, social, in-person event on the calendar.
cards.how_to_join: Create a free Meetup account, join the group that fits, RSVP to the next swap event.
cards.notes: Joining and attending public groups is free; a few organizers collect a small event fee, shown up front.

cards.title: Be My Eyes (volunteer from your phone)
cards.blurb: Answer live video calls from blind and low-vision users who need a second pair of eyes to sort mail or match colors.
cards.who_for: Anyone with a smartphone and a few spare minutes; perfect for people who want to give a skill without scheduling anything.
cards.how_to_join: Download Be My Eyes, pick "volunteer", enable notifications, answer calls when convenient (or ignore them).
cards.notes: Completely free; the app earns nothing from you.

cards.title: Museum/docent and historical-society volunteer lists
cards.blurb: Small museums and historical societies are always short on people to give tours, fix displays, or scan archives - and they train you for free.
cards.who_for: History buffs and people who love teaching small crowds.
cards.how_to_join: Find a local historical society, hunt for a "get involved" or "volunteer" page, email the coordinator named there.
cards.notes: Free; background checks are sometimes required for certain roles, at no cost to you.
